name: Gorrin Teague
title: the Cabbage Man
why: Beside the east road to Mistmere Harbor. He was taking cabbages to the Tide Market, and this is where the cart stopped.
examine: Gorrin Teague sells cabbages from a handcart. The cart is never the same cart twice. Nobody has remarked on it.
He counts his cabbages out loud, twice, and is never pleased with either number.
Behind him on the road is a trail of cabbage leaves. He says it helps him find his way back.
meet: Good morning. I was taking cabbages to the Tide Market. The cabbages were on the cart. The cart was on the road. I had assumed the road was on my side.
Gorrin Teague. Cabbages. Some days a cart.

wary: Cabbages? No. Then I can’t help you.
neutral: Morning. Mind the leaves. They’re most of the second load.
warm: Good. You’re here. I kept you a cabbage. It’s only mostly squashed.
fond: You came back. People don’t, as a rule. They’ve seen the cart.

tired: I’ve talked a great deal. Come back tomorrow. I expect to have lost something new by then.
finished: That’s everything. Except the cabbages. There are always the cabbages.

say: It was a good cart. Two wheels, most of a bench, and no brakes. Then the hill. Then the hill again.

options.text: Oh no. Are you all right?
reply: Nobody asks that. They ask after the cabbages.

options.text: I’ll watch the cart while you look.
reply: Do. Watch it closely. It has been known to leave.

say: I lost four hundred and eleven cabbages this year. I count them. Somebody should.

reply: It is. Thank you. Most people say it’s a lot to lose.

options.text: I’ll count the next batch with you.
reply: Eleven is my lucky number. It hasn’t been lucky yet.

options.text: Have you tried a stronger cart?
reply: I don’t grow cabbages, they just kinda show up.

options.text: You lose them because you drive downhill.

say: Every Sunday I think, this week the cabbages arrive. Every Sunday they arrive in a different way.

options.text: What are they like when they arrive?
Let me carry the next load.
reply: You’re lighter than the cart. You also don’t roll.

options.text: What do you call a lost cabbage? A head of state.
reply: Is that a real thing? It sounds real. I’ll put it on the cart.

say: I’ll tell you a secret. I like selling cabbages. Someone hands me a coin and gets a cabbage. Nothing else is involved. I find it restful.

reply: Take two. They’re from the good batch. The good batch stayed on the cart.

options.text: Nobody was ever fooled by a cabbage.
reply: Not once. Even the ones that looked like lettuce confessed.

errand.title: A wheel for the cart
offer: The cart needs a wheel. A wheel is mostly wood. I have cabbages.
Six birch would do it. I’d get them myself, but I’d have to leave the cart, and then it would leave too.
waiting: No birch yet. That’s all right. The cart can’t go anywhere. It has one wheel.
done: Six. I counted twice and got six both times. That has never happened.
Have a cabbage. It’s from the good batch.

keepsake.name: A cabbage
keepsake.text: From the good batch. The good batch stayed on the cart.

memories.asked-after-him: You asked if he was all right before you asked about the cabbages. He is still thinking about it.
memories.counted-together: You offered to count the next batch with him. Eleven is his lucky number. It hasn’t been lucky yet.
memories.asked-about-the-arrivals: You asked what the cabbages are like when they arrive. He had not been asked before.
memories.honest-trade: You called selling cabbages an honest trade. He has written it on the cart.
memories.brought-the-birch: You brought him six birch for a wheel. He counted twice and got six both times.

early: A camp. I only have cabbages to bring. Ask me when we know each other better. Or when I’ve sold some.
ask: A camp. With a fire. I could keep a cabbage patch.
I’d bring the cart if it behaved. It won’t, but I’d bring it.
yes: Then it’s settled. I’ll bring the cabbages. I’ll bring most of them.
full: There’s no bed free. I sleep badly on a cabbage in any case. Send word when there’s room.
camp.role: Tends a cabbage patch by the fire.
